quran.note: Lut tells his people they commit an immorality no one before them did; he and his family are saved except his wife; a rain of stones falls.
The angels come to Lut; he is anguished for his guests; “If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support”; the angels say they are messengers of his Lord.
The people of the city come rejoicing; Lut asks them not to shame him before his guests; the shriek seizes them at sunrise and the city is turned upside down.
Lut, a trustworthy messenger, warns them; he and his family are saved except an old woman who remained behind.
Lut’s people; Ibrahim says “within it is Lot”; the angels say they will save him and his family except his wife; a sign is left.
Lut’s people deny the warning; they demanded his guests; Allah obliterated their eyes.
The wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut as an example of those who disbelieved.

hadith.summary: The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah’s mercy on Lut, who sought refuge in a strong support. The same report has his remark about being more deserving of doubt than Ibrahim, and about Yusuf’s long stay in prison.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: On “Here are my daughters”: records Mujahid that the women were not Lut’s own daughters but women of his nation, because every prophet is like a father to his people, with a similar saying from Qatadah and others. The abridged text adds that Lut was directing them toward their wives and cites 26:165-166 and 15:70-72. It records Ibn Abbas and others that “a trying day” meant a hard test, because he knew he had to defend his guests.
